methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio spiked from 6.70% (FY2023) to 11.40% (FY2024) — the sharpest single-year jump in this bank's 15-year record — but then IMPROVED to 8.38% (FY2025), unlike the continued deterioration seen at AB Bank and Al-Arafah Islami Bank over the same period. Still meaningfully above the 2017-2021 average of ~4.5%.

ROE reached 13.29% in FY2025, its best level in the entire 2011-2025 series except for the anomalous 19.61% in FY2011 — recovering from 9.04% (FY2024) and 8.24% (FY2023) even as NPLs rose, driven by strong growth in investment income (BDT 26.4bn in FY2025 vs BDT 14.3bn FY2024).

Capital Adequacy Ratio has stayed in a healthy 11-18% band throughout 2011-2025 (15.32% at FY2025), never approaching the regulatory minimum even during the FY2024 NPL spike — capital strength has not been a constraint here, unlike at AB Bank (CAR went negative) or Al-Arafah (CAR declined toward its floor).

Credit-Deposit Ratio (this bank's LDR) fell sharply from 72.48% (FY2023) to 55.77% (FY2025) even as both loans and deposits grew — deposits (BDT 456.5bn FY2025) grew much faster than loans (BDT 294.7bn FY2025), indicating the bank has been building a larger liquidity buffer / investment book rather than accelerating lending, consistent with the large jump in the 'Investments' line (BDT 219.8bn FY2025 vs BDT 102.8bn FY2022).

Net interest income collapsed and turned structurally NEGATIVE starting in 2025, on a separate/solo basis - a pattern invisible in the annual-only dataset before this session's quarterly deepening pass. Discrete quarterly NII: BDT 1.57bn (2024 Q3) -> BDT 0.06bn (2025 Q1, near zero) -> BDT -1.19bn (2025 Q2) -> BDT -0.97bn (2025 Q3) -> BDT -0.38bn (2026 Q1) -> BDT -1.75bn (2026 Q2) - five consecutive quarters of near-zero-or-negative NII. This is confirmed independently at the FULL-YEAR level by the FY2025 annual report's own summary table: Interest Income BDT 28,698.96m vs Interest Expense BDT 30,076.05m, i.e. a full-year NII of BDT -1,377.09m - the two independently-sourced figures (quarterly interims vs annual report) corroborate each other. The bank has stayed profitable through this (NPAT positive in 4 of these 6 quarters) only because investment income and fee/commission income have more than offset the negative interest margin - a materially riskier earnings mix than the NII-driven profitability typical of the 2014-2023 period in this same dataset.

2024 Q3 (discrete, separate basis) shows a rare pattern: profit before tax was still positive at BDT 346.8m, but a current-tax charge of BDT 1.38bn for that single quarter (as printed in the filing's own 'July to Sep 2024' column - not a figure this dataset derived by subtraction) exceeded pre-tax profit outright, producing a discrete-quarter NET LOSS of BDT -1,033.2m despite the operating business being profitable that quarter. The cumulative Jan-Sep 2024 figures were still comfortably profitable (PBT BDT 4,378.7m, NPAT BDT 1,978.7m), so this is a single-quarter tax-timing effect, not a sign of operating distress - but it illustrates that this bank's tax provisioning is lumpy across quarters within a year and any quarter-only (non-cumulative) reading of profitability here can be misleading without checking the cumulative column too.

historical_context: Bank Asia shows a materially different trajectory from AB Bank (ABBANK) and Al-Arafah Islami Bank (ALARABANK) over the same 2023-2025 window covered so far in this dataset: all three banks saw NPL ratios rise in FY2024 (part of the broader 2024-2025 Bangladesh banking-sector asset-quality stress), but Bank Asia's rise was smaller, and its FY2025 ROE and CAR both improved rather than continuing to deteriorate. This is an early, genuine example of the cross-bank differentiation this project is meant to surface — not every DSE bank experienced the crisis the same way. The 2026-08-26 quarterly deepening pass (2014-2025 Q1-Q3, 32 new quarters) revealed that Bank Asia's FY2025 profitability recovery (noted above) coexists with a much less healthy underlying trend once viewed at quarterly resolution: net interest income - the core, most durable source of bank earnings - went structurally negative for 5 of the last 6 quarters on record (2025 Q2 through 2026 Q2). The annual figures alone would not have surfaced this; it only became visible once Q1-Q3 data existed to compare against Q4/annual.
data_gaps: 2026-08-26 update: this session extracted 32 additional quarters (2014 Q1-Q3, 2015 Q1-Q2, 2016 Q1-Q3, 2017 Q1-Q3, 2018 Q1 and Q3, 2019-2025 Q1-Q3), bringing Q1-Q3 coverage to essentially complete for 2016-2025 and largely complete back to 2014. Genuine remaining gaps, not fabricated or annual-backfilled: 2010-2013 entirely, 2015 Q3, and 2018 Q2 - every candidate URL for these 404s on the live bankasia-bd.com site AND on Wayback Machine's playback layer (confirmed across 2 retry rounds this session, even though Wayback's own CDX index lists captures for all of them), so this is a persistent access blocker worth re-checking in a future session rather than a research gap. NPL/CAR/provision-coverage/ROA/ROE were not computed for any Q1-Q3 quarter (this dataset's usual annualization/averaging convention for these ratios is not yet defined for quarterly cadence, and asset-quality figures are not disclosed in these unaudited interim statements) - only total_assets, gross_loans, total_deposits, equity, LDR (calculated), EPS, and YoY growth are populated for the new quarterly periods in ratios_timeseries.json. Q2 2026 remains on a CONSOLIDATED basis (only version published at retrieval time) while every other period including all newly-added ones is separate/solo - not directly comparable without adjustment.
